editorial.headline: The Retail Code for the Details That Complete an Outfit
editorial.standfirst: For apparel accessories and their small but essential components, this activity is nationally open to full foreign ownership—yet unavailable for PMA registration in Bali today.
editorial.body:
This activity covers specialised retail of clothing accessories: scarves, head coverings, handkerchiefs, headbands, traditional blangkon caps, peci, hats, ties, belts, face veils, gloves, socks, towels and blankets. Its remit also extends to the practical retail trade in garment buttons, zippers and sewing thread. In other words, it is a code for the retail details around clothing—items that finish an outfit, serve a daily function, or enable its repair and assembly.

The activity is open across the full business-scale range recorded here: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. That breadth matters because the scope accommodates both a compact specialist shop and a more substantial retail operation without changing the essential character of the trade. The defining feature is not a particular product aesthetic or customer segment, but the specialised retail sale of apparel accessories and the small components associated with clothing.

At the national level, the position is direct. The activity is marked TERBUKA for PMA and permits a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. A foreign investor can therefore hold the entire national ownership interest available under this record. The applicable PMA source is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no need to soften that national reading: the record describes an activity open to foreign investment at the full stated ceiling.

Bali requires a different conclusion. A foreigner cannot register this activity in Bali today. The Bali status is BLOCCATO_CLASSE_RISCHIO because, at the Besar scale, the OSS risk classification is Rendah or Menengah-Rendah across every scope. Bali’s island-wide, permanent moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, and this record identifies the block as applying from May 13, 2026. That does not alter the national 100% ceiling; it determines whether the nationally open activity can be registered as PMA in Bali. For a founder planning around Bali, the practical position is therefore clear: national openness exists, but Bali PMA registration is blocked under the stated moratorium.
